venture.name: Jewelry Travel Organizer
venture.working_site_name: Jewelry / Journey (working concept name, not a confirmed brand)
venture.concept: A compact travel organizer designed to reduce jewelry movement, tangling and damage.
venture.primary_product: Book-style travel jewelry organizer with secured storage by jewelry type.
venture.target_customers: Proposed primary audience: women ages 18–54 who travel and wear jewelry; secondary audience: gift buyers. These are targeting hypotheses, not measured buyers.
venture.needs: Protect meaningful jewelry, pack efficiently, find pieces quickly and avoid tangled necklaces.
venture.value_proposition: Visible, secure retention along necklaces and bracelets, plus dedicated earring and bangle storage.
venture.geographic_market: United States is the initial research market; a launch territory has not been finalized.
venture.distribution: Direct online sales through the venture website are a planning assumption; no established sales channel was verified.
features: Paired small snap-closed supports along both sides of necklaces
Separate storage for studs, drops and hoops
Book-like extra page for bangles and larger hoops
Protective dividers and durable closures, subject to prototype testing
venture.unknowns: Final brand, materials, dimensions, capacity, manufacturing costs, shipping policy, demand and selling price are not finalized.
venture.context: Travel cases are direct alternatives; improvised pouches and jewelry bags are indirect substitutes. This price sample focuses on four direct competitors.
venture.prior_research: User-provided research describes 80 reviews of a competing Amazon product: 59 positive, 15 mixed and 6 negative; 7 mentioned faulty snaps. These are not reviews of this venture and were not recollected for this pricing mission. Simulated focus-group responses are fictional, not customer demand evidence.

comparison.interpretation: The premium WOLF starting price raises the four-brand mean. The three core alternatives are clustered near $40–$69; their median is $40. Promotional and unavailable offers remain only in the full researched-offer range.

preliminary_pricing_recommendation.rationale: Near but above BAGSMART Crush ($39.99) and Quince ($40), below Mark & Graham ($69), and well below WOLF ($225 starting price). Extra retention and durable closures must demonstrate value to justify a premium over $40 alternatives.
conditions: Prototype-test necklace retention and snap durability
Estimate landed cost, packaging, fulfillment, returns and contribution margin
Test $45, $49 and $59 with intended buyers; measure purchase intent and conversion
Set shipping and personalization policies before final pricing

market_opportunities: Demonstrate reduced necklace movement with paired supports along the chain. Existing organizers already claim tangle protection; an evidence-based demonstration is more defensible than claiming the category lacks it.
Make reliable, replaceable closures a design priority. The user’s earlier competitor-review sample raises a snap concern, but does not establish its market-wide frequency.
Explore an optional bangle/large-hoop page or gift package after cost testing. Treat bundles and personalization as concepts, not observed venture offers.
Use clear storage demonstrations and a compact packing video to explain the functional difference. Avoid an absolute guarantee that jewelry can never tangle.
research_limitations: Eight selected offers from four direct competitors are a purposive sample, not a market census or a sales-weighted average. Brand ranges cover only researched offers, not entire catalogs.
Prices were checked on 2026-10-27 through retrieved official pages. Some indexed pages were several days or weeks old. Prices, promotions and availability can change; no checkout was performed.

Comparisons use USD merchandise prices for one organizer before tax, shipping and personalization. Size, capacity, materials and brand equity differ; these are functional alternatives, not identical products.
WOLF prices are explicitly starting prices. Configured WOLF stock and Mark & Graham color stock were not established. Dazzling is unavailable in the observed variant.
BAGSMART crossed-out prices are displayed reference prices, not evidence they were historically charged. Quince traditional retail is not its own regular price.
Brand protection claims were not tested. The absence of a feature in retrieved descriptions does not prove no competitor offers it. Mark & Graham detail extraction was incomplete.
No manufacturing costs, willingness-to-pay study, sales volumes, conversion rates or profitability data were available. Recommended pricing is a hypothesis, not an optimal price.
